questions.stem: What is a domain in Microsoft Fabric?

options.text: A capacity reserved for a single department, used to isolate its compute from other teams
A logical grouping of workspaces, usually by business area, used to organize and govern data
A network boundary that blocks traffic between workspaces that belong to different business units
A special type of lakehouse that holds the master data shared by all workspaces in the tenant

questions.explanation: Domains group workspaces by business area, such as Sales or Finance, so data can be organized and governed the way the business is, in the spirit of data mesh.

questions.stem: Which role can create a new domain?

options.text: Any user with a Pro license
Any workspace admin
A Fabric administrator
Any workspace contributor

questions.explanation: Fabric administrators create domains and assign their domain admins. Domain admins and contributors then manage the domain and assign workspaces to it.

questions.stem: A workspace admin is a contributor of the Finance domain and wants their workspace to belong to it. Where do they do this?

options.text: In each item's settings, by setting the domain on items one by one
In the workspace's settings, by choosing the Finance domain
In the capacity settings of the capacity that hosts the workspace
Only by asking Microsoft Support to move the workspace into the domain

questions.explanation: Domain contributors can assign workspaces they are admins of to the domain from the workspace's own settings.

questions.stem: Which two are benefits of organizing workspaces into domains? Each correct answer is a complete solution.

options.text: Workspaces in a domain no longer need capacity
People can find data by business area, for example by filtering the OneLake catalog by domain
Domain admins can manage some settings for their own domain instead of the whole tenant
Every user in a domain becomes an admin of its workspaces
Data in a domain is encrypted with a key only that domain holds

questions.explanation: Domains help people discover data by business area and let some governance be delegated to domain admins. They don't grant workspace roles, add encryption or remove the need for capacity.

questions.stem: A domain admin of the Sales domain wants to add a colleague as a second domain admin of Sales. Who can do this?

options.text: The current domain admin, from the Domains tab
Any workspace admin of a workspace in the domain
A domain contributor, from the workspace settings
A Fabric admin

questions.explanation: Fabric admins specify domain admins. Domain admins can define contributors and edit the description, but they can't add or delete other domain admins.

questions.stem: The Finance domain has a subdomain named Payroll. Who are the domain admins of Payroll?

options.text: The domain contributors of the Finance domain
Users a Fabric admin assigns to Payroll separately
The domain admins of the parent Finance domain
The workspace admins of the workspaces in Payroll

questions.explanation: Subdomains don't have their own domain admins. They use the admins of their parent domain.

questions.stem: A Fabric admin assigns the Sales domain to every workspace on the Sales capacity. Next week a new workspace is created on that capacity. What is its domain?

options.text: It joins the Sales domain automatically, because capacity assignment covers future workspaces
It isn't affected: assignment by capacity applies only to workspaces that existed at the time
It is blocked from being created on the capacity until a domain admin approves its domain
It joins the Sales domain after the next daily sync between the capacity and domain settings

questions.explanation: Assigning by capacity affects existing workspaces only. A workspace assigned to the capacity later must be assigned some other way, for example through a default domain.

questions.stem: Every new workspace created by members of the Marketing security group must land in the Marketing domain without anyone assigning it. What do you configure?

options.text: Assign the Marketing domain by capacity once a week to catch new ones
Make every member of the Marketing group a domain admin of Marketing
Make Marketing the default domain for the Marketing security group
Assign the Marketing domain to workspaces by matching the workspace name

questions.explanation: A default domain assigns new workspaces created by the specified users or groups to that domain. Assigning by name or capacity only covers workspaces that already exist.

questions.stem: Which two tenant-level settings can a domain admin override for their own domain when the tenant admin delegates them? Each correct answer is a complete solution.

options.text: The Git provider the domain's workspaces connect to
The certification settings, including which experts can certify items
The workspace roles of every user in the domain
A default sensitivity label for items in the domain's workspaces
The capacity that the domain's workspaces run on

questions.explanation: Delegated domain settings include a domain-level default sensitivity label and certification settings such as the certifiers. Workspace roles, capacities and Git connections aren't domain settings.

questions.stem: A workspace is assigned to the Finance domain. A manager asks whether this now lets everyone in Finance open the workspace's lakehouse. What is the answer?

options.text: No, only domain admins get access to the domain's items
No, domain assignment doesn't change who can see or access items
Yes, domain members get Viewer access to every workspace in the domain
Yes, but only for items endorsed as Master data

questions.explanation: Access still comes from workspace roles and item permissions. Domains organize and govern workspaces but don't grant access.
